excerpt: 1 SPECIAL TOPICS COMPUTER-ASSISTED REPORTING JOU 3950 COURSE SYLLABUS Fall 2012 PROFESSOR Joe Gisondi EMAIL jgisondi@gmail.com OFFICE/HOURS Buzzard Hall, room 2546 MW 2:30-3:30 p.m. W 10-11 a.m. R 2:40-3:40 p.m. Available other times by appointment PHONE 581-6003 TEXTS The Art of Access (David Cuillier and Charles N. Davis) COURSE DESCRIPTION To give students the fundamentals of computer-assisted reporting, using public documents in order to gather, organize, evaluate data to write objective reports in accepted journalistic style across several media platforms. COURSE OBJECTIVES By the conclusion of JOU 3000, students will: 1. demonstrate advanced news-writing skills, citing public documents to develop news stories; 2. demonstrate advanced news-gathering, research methods and interviewing skills, focusing on where and how to find information through public data and documents; 3. demonstrate the ability to provide background in public affairs reporting, through government statistics and other data; 4. demonstrate an advanced awareness for accuracy and fairness; 5. demonstrate an advanced awareness of legal and ethical issues affecting news-gathering and reporting; 6. demonstrate a sensitivity in coverage of diverse cultures and populations ACADEMIC HONESTY Plagiarism is the unpardonable sin of journalism, an act that essentially ends a journalist’s career. There is nothing wrong with using information from another source so long as it is clearly credited within the story. If you take a quote or information from another publication, cite it within the story. An assignment determined to be plagiarized will be given a grade of “0” and the responsible student will receive an “F” for the course. Plus, this student will be referred to the appropriate EIU board for discipline. According to the university’s policy, students who plagiarize are eligible for dismissal from EIU. STUDENTS WITH DISABILITIES Contact the Office of Disability Services (581-6583) for answers regarding accommodations, auxiliary learning aids and physical accessibility. Diagnostic information regarding the disability must be submitted so the most appropriate accommodations can be arranged. Refer to the Undergraduate Catalog for more information. 2 ABSENCES & MAKE-UP WORK Students are expected to be in class on time and remain until the dismissal. Attendance is essential in this class where both the professor and visiting journalists will train students on ways to gather data from public documents. If you miss a class meeting, you will fail to learn the skills necessary to complete your assignment. So, please, make sure you attend each class. Ten points will be deducted from your attendance for each day missed. ASSIGNMENTS Name Points Research Project 300 Quizzes/Reports 100 Exercises 100 Attendance 100 Total 600 DEADLINES – Making deadlines are essential in journalism. In this class, missing deadline will mean the final published project gets delayed both in print and online. There are not excuses for failing to do the assigned task on time. So please start working early and often on your individual tasks as they relate to our final project. __________________________________________________________________ FORMAT – All assignments are required to be typed and double-spaced in 12-point Times New Roman, have one-inch margins on all sides, and be stapled
